the use of a unique, low dose (LD) of enoxaparin during percutaneous coronary treatment (PCI) can be a safe and efficient method of anticoagulation for patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) and a high risk of bleeding, including those that are elderly or have a reduced renal function.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of low molecular weight heparins in patients undergoing PCI with stenting is not recommended, because of a high risk of bleeding complications, especially in patients with an elevated bleeding risk.
the low-dose enoxaparin regimen is safe and efficacious in elective PCI, with no increase in major bleeding.
the combination of low-dose aspirin and low-dose clopidogrel is associated with a higher rate of bleeding than aspirin alone in patients undergoing PCI, with or without stent implantation.
